summary:
NASA operates two satellite systems — MODIS and VIIRS — that detect active fires globally. When their data is merged directly, the same fire gets counted multiple times, creating false spikes and misleading statistics. No existing public tool solves this problem.

FireWatch AI is an open-source geospatial intelligence platform that harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire data using a scientific clustering algorithm — removing double-counted detections and preserving accurate fire records across 26 years of NASA observations.

The platform features a 3D WebGL Earth globe with live NASA fire data, a 6-mode meteorological overlay showing wind, temperature, humidity, rain, pressure, and cloud cover simultaneously with fire activity, a burning activity calendar, and a statistical anomaly detection engine that automatically flags unusual fire events.

Built on FastAPI and React 18, the system delivers satellite fire tiles in under 10 milliseconds using a two-tier RAM and disk cache, with a database of 230,000+ authentic fire detections.

FireWatch AI transforms raw, incompatible satellite observations into unified, scientifically traceable fire intelligence — giving disaster management authorities and forest departments a single reliable platform for real-time fire monitoring and historical analysis.
details:
FireWatch AI is an open-source geospatial intelligence platform that solves a critical scientific problem in satellite fire monitoring. NASA operates two satellite systems — MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2011) — that both detect active fires globally. When their raw data is merged directly, the same fire gets counted 2 to 4 times, creating artificial spikes, false statistics, and unreliable historical records across 26 years of data. No existing public tool resolves this problem.

What it does: FireWatch AI harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire detections using a Haversine spatial clustering algorithm with anti-chain bridging bounds, eliminating double-counted observations while preserving sensor-specific Fire Radiative Power independently — never summing physically incompatible measurements across sensors.

Key features: A native 3D WebGL Earth globe with live NASA FIRMS fire data delivered in under 10 milliseconds using a two-tier RAM and SSD tile cache. A Windy-style 6-mode meteorological overlay (wind, temperature, rain, humidity, pressure, cloud cover) powered by Open-Meteo NWP, allowing users to correlate fire activity with live weather conditions. A burning activity calendar visualizing 26 years of fire history. A MAD statistical anomaly detection engine that automatically flags unusual fire events using Modified Z-scores.

Intended impact: FireWatch AI gives disaster management authorities, forest departments, and climate researchers a single scientifically reliable platform for real-time fire monitoring and historical analysis — replacing fragmented, double-counted raw satellite feeds with unified, traceable fire intelligence.

Tools and technologies: Python, FastAPI, SQLite WAL, React 18, TypeScript, MapLibre GL, NASA FIRMS API, NASA GIBS WMTS, Open-Meteo NWP API, Vite, Pytest. Database contains 230,844 authentic active-fire detections. 19 out of 19 automated tests passing.

Creativity: FireWatch AI is the only open platform that mathematically resolves MODIS-VIIRS double-counting, provides satellite blind window alerts showing when fire status is unknown between orbital passes, and delivers fire intelligence with simultaneous live meteorological context — all in a single unified interface.
